name: Cuba
intro: It's 1953. You're 26, a lawyer, and you've just decided to attack an army barracks with 130 friends. Cuba is a casino for Americans and a sugar plantation for their companies; Batista took power in a coup. Ninety miles away sits the most powerful country on earth. You will play the revolution — and then the state it builds. Every choice will be watched from Washington and Moscow. Choose how small a country stands up.

nodes.title: Moncada
nodes.situation: Attack the Moncada barracks, or build a political movement and wait for elections Batista may never hold?

choices.label: Attack
choices.summary: Attack

effects.text: The attack fails; 60 rebels are tortured and killed; Castro's trial speech, "History will absolve me," makes him famous
effects.insight: failure as marketing

effects.text: Exiled, you meet an Argentine doctor named Guevara
effects.insight: the revolution gets its second face

effects.text: The Eisenhower administration keeps arming Batista
effects.insight: the US chooses the devil it knows

effects.insight: repression recruits for you

effects.text: Latin American students take note
effects.insight: armed struggle becomes a template.

effects.insight: quiet contacts begin

effects.text: No exile; no Che
effects.insight: the revolution, if it comes, is Cuban and moderate

nodes.title: Whose Sugar?
nodes.situation: You've nationalized US oil refineries that refused Soviet crude. Washington cuts the sugar quota. Moscow offers to buy it. Exiles are training in Guatemala. Do you go all in with the Soviets?

choices.label: Nationalize Everything, Take the Soviet Deal
choices.summary: Nationalize Everything, Take the Soviet Deal

effects.text: The US embargo begins (1960) and never ends
effects.insight: 60+ years

effects.text: The CIA's 1,400 exiles are crushed in 72 hours
effects.insight: Kennedy is humiliated; you're a hero

effects.text: Khrushchev adopts Cuba as proof revolution can happen without the Red Army
effects.insight: and as a base

effects.text: 200,000 leave in two years
effects.insight: Cuba loses its professional class

effects.text: Latin American leftists take the "Cuban road"; the US answers with the Alliance for Progress and a wave of coups.
effects.insight: Partners judge a commitment by what it costs you to keep it. A changed commitment reshapes their choices.

choices.label: Nationalize With Compensation, Stay Non-Aligned
choices.summary: Nationalize With Compensation, Stay Non-Aligned

effects.text: Kennedy's liberals argue for coexistence; the embargo is partial
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

effects.text: You join the Non-Aligned Movement as a founder (as you did in 1961)
effects.insight: but this time it means it

effects.text: Khrushchev is disappointed; no missiles ever come
effects.insight: A threat to one side changes the other side’s calculations, encouraging it to build or seek protection.

effects.text: Slower socialism, a freer press, a mixed economy
effects.insight: Cuba as Latin Yugoslavia

effects.text: Mexico becomes your model and protector
effects.insight: Latin nationalism, not Soviet communism.

choices.label: Strike First
choices.summary: Strike First — Attack the Exile Camps in Guatemala

effects.text: A Cuban raid on a US-backed camp; Guatemala declares war

effects.text: Eisenhower authorizes open US military action
effects.insight: no Bay of Pigs fiasco, a real invasion

effects.text: The revolution fights a US landing; tens of thousands die; you're captured or in the hills

effects.text: Khrushchev protests and does nothing
effects.insight: Cuba was never worth a war before the missiles

effects.text: Latin America condemns you
effects.insight: the OAS backs the US.

nodes.title: The Missiles
nodes.situation: Khrushchev offers to place nuclear missiles in Cuba. They'd deter a US invasion. They'd also make you the world's target. Che says yes; some in your circle say the Soviets will trade you away.

choices.label: Accept the Missiles
choices.summary: Accept the Missiles

effects.text: Thirteen days; Moscow settles without asking you
effects.insight: you learn you're a chess piece

effects.text: The no-invasion pledge is why your government survives to 2016 and beyond
effects.insight: Foreign decisions alter domestic coalitions. Leaders must answer to the institutions and people keeping them in power.

effects.text: Khrushchev falls in 1964; Brezhnev keeps you as a subsidized showcase
effects.insight: $5 billion a year by the 1980s

effects.text: Frustrated with Moscow's caution, Che goes to export revolution alone
effects.insight: he's killed in 1967

effects.text: Exiles feel betrayed by Kennedy
effects.insight: the lobby that shapes US policy for 60 years hardens.

choices.label: Refuse the Missiles
choices.summary: Refuse the Missiles — Ask for Conventional Arms Only

effects.text: No missile crisis; Kennedy, without a "win," authorizes Operation Mongoose to escalate
effects.insight: a second invasion attempt in 1963 (40%)

effects.text: Khrushchev respects the refusal but funds you less
effects.insight: Cuba is poorer, freer of Moscow

effects.text: No thirteen days; the world never learns Cuba's name the same way
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

effects.text: The Non-Aligned Movement embraces you as a non-nuclear stand.
effects.insight: A threat to one side changes the other side’s calculations, encouraging it to build or seek protection.

choices.label: Accept AND Demand Cuban Control of the Warheads
choices.summary: Accept AND Demand Cuban Control of the Warheads

effects.text: Khrushchev refuses
effects.insight: but the request leaks; Washington now believes Castro might launch

effects.text: Airstrikes are approved
effects.insight: the crisis has no back-channel because Moscow can't promise you'll obey

chance.successText: A nuclear weapon is used. The crisis has crossed a threshold; leaders now face the danger of a wider exchange.
chance.failureText: Leaders stop short of nuclear use in this run. The confrontation still damages trust and raises the risk of another crisis.

effects.text: You prepare to die "with honor"
effects.insight: 100,000 militia on the beaches

effects.text: Mao praises you as the true revolutionary
effects.insight: the Sino-Soviet split pulls at Cuba

effects.text: Latin America is terrified; the OAS expels you (it did anyway) and backs a quarantine.
effects.insight: A choice in one capital changes the options available elsewhere. Local leaders respond to the new balance of risk and opportunity.

variants.situation: Your non-aligned policy has kept some distance from Moscow. Now a Soviet military offer tests that independence. Accepting missiles would reverse your earlier course.

nodes.title: Special Period
nodes.situation: Gorbachev is cutting subsidies. Your top general, Ochoa, is on trial (drugs, or a warning to reformers). The Eastern bloc has fallen. When the USSR ends, 85% of your trade vanishes overnight.

effects.text: Blackouts, bicycles, oxen
